title: Sensorless Six-Step Commutation
text: Use six-step commutation to run a BLDC motor or PMSM using sensorless control, 6 inputs, 4 outputs; {Alignment} determines initial rotor position by checking rotor, {Alignment -> Open-loop run} determines rotor position by starting the motor, {Alignment -> Open-loop run -> Controlled commutation} determines rotor position by running the motor, {Number of motor pole pairs}, {Discrete step size (s)} sets the sample time after which block executes again, {Alignment duty cycle} sets the duty cycle of voltage to be applied between phases, {Alignment time} sets the duration to apply the voltage between phase, {Open-loop duty cycle (range: [0,1])} sets the duty cycle of voltage to be applied to all three, {Target open-loop speed (RPM)} sets the target speed, {Ramp up time to reach target open-loop speed (s)}, {Open-loop speed to initiate transition to controlled commutation (RPM)} sets the speed at which the algorithm starts motor phase voltage acquisition process during open-loop, {Speed samples required to complete transition to controlled commutation} sets the minimum number of speed samples to be considered before transitioning to controlled commutation, {Compensation for filter delay (Tf) and demagnetization time (Td)} sets the one of the two methods to define compensation for T f and T d Specify via, {Time delay due to voltage sense filter, Tf (s)} sets the time delay to compensate for delay due to a hardware or software filter used for voltage measurement and {Demagnetization time, Td (s)} sets the time during which the demagnetization of winding is occurring and voltage signals need not be acquired. Values come from the instance.
